summary: This sermon explores baptism through the story of Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch in Acts 8, emphasizing that baptism is the culmination of believers' obedience—both those who share the gospel and the new believer who publicly declares faith. The pastor walks through how baptism starts with obedient witness, is built on clear gospel understanding, and ends with a new believer's step of obedience.
key_points: Baptism starts with an obedient believer willing to share the gospel
Baptism is built on a clear understanding of Jesus's message and substitutionary atonement
Baptism ends with a new believer's public declaration of faith
Baptism results from many small acts of obedience by believers planting gospel seeds
Baptism is the beginning of discipleship, not the end
big_idea: Baptism is the culmination of believers' obedience—both those who faithfully share the gospel and the new believer who publicly declares their commitment to follow Jesus.
title: Baptism: A Fresh Perspective
